## Standards

Standards sources: `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, plus the supplied smell baseline.

### Hard violations

1. **`src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:376-380` violates the `README.md` Reviewer contract.** README requires every accepted leg to grant “exactly that one byte-exact command.” The check only requires inclusion of the canonical diff and permits additional ceiling-authorized commands:

```ts
!grant.bashCommands.includes(range.diffCommand) ||
grant.bashCommands.some((command) =>
  !capabilities.bashCommands.includes(command))
```

Thus `bashCommands: [range.diffCommand, "other ceiling command"]` can be accepted and exposed to the child.

2. **`src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:212-215` does not fully enforce README’s “unavailable host tools … fail closed” rule.** Host availability is checked only for tools requested by a proposal:

```ts
tools.some((tool) =>
  !ceiling.tools.includes(tool) || !hostTools.includes(tool))
```

A capability file may contain an unavailable tool while a narrower proposal omits it, allowing activation and dispatch rather than rejecting the invalid invocation ceiling.

### Judgement call

- **Possible Primitive Obsession — `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:278-288`.** Although `ReviewerPreflightViolation` and `PreflightViolation` exist, most domain failures are communicated as generic `Error` strings and recovered through regexes such as `/material|UTF-8/i` and `/capability|bash commands/i`. This makes classification dependent on message wording. Prefer carrying the closed violation code through typed errors at validation boundaries.

No scratch artifacts or probe changes were created during this review leg.

## Spec

- **[P1] Schema-invalid sibling calls can crash after acceptance instead of closing cleanly.**

  > “Once accepted, all later proposals are rejected.”
  > “No correction or second batch is then legal.”

  `src/reviewer-role.ts:84-90` records every schema-rejected `Agent` transport event as `transport-rejected`, but `src/reviewer-execution-ledger.ts:103` throws if that event arrives after acceptance. Thus, if a model emits one valid atomic proposal alongside a malformed sibling and the valid call accepts first, the malformed call’s terminal event throws rather than becoming bounded no-start/closed evidence. This creates ordering-dependent infrastructure failure after the sole batch has already started. Existing tests cover transport rejection before corrected acceptance, but not this post-acceptance ordering.

No scratch artifacts or probe changes were created. The pinned target and supplied diff command were inspected; additional test commands were unavailable under the accepted bash grant.

Summary: Standards — 3 findings; worst: accepted legs can receive extra bash commands contrary to the exact-command contract. Spec — 1 finding; worst: a malformed sibling call can cause an ordering-dependent post-acceptance infrastructure failure.
